According to a new report from Bloomberg, Apple is less than two weeks away from unveiling a brand-new smart display. The report also shed additional light on the design details of Apple's highly anticipated smart home hub.

Bloomberg reports that the home hub will feature a 6-inch square display, with an overall aesthetic that calls to mind the classic iMac G4—a design known for its hemispherical base with a metal arm holding the display aloft.

According to Mark Gurman, the device is "roughly as thick as an iPhone," with bezels resembling the quarter-inch black borders found on older iPad models. The body features rounded corners and is "completely devoid of sharp edges."

Here are more design details mentioned in the report:

  • The body uses Apple's "standard gray aluminum casing," with a "rubber coating on the bottom to keep it firmly planted on a tabletop."
  • It includes a USB-C port for power, with no built-in battery, meaning it must remain plugged in at all times.
  • The device sits on a "metal circular base featuring multiple rings of speaker perforations."
  • The display is connected to the base via a "polished metal arm."
  • Users can tilt the display forward or backward.
  • There are no volume buttons or power buttons on the device.
  • The front houses a FaceTime camera, while there is no camera on the back.

Bloomberg also mentions another version of the home hub, "designed to be mounted on a wall." This version also draws power via USB-C and features a "slim square base below the display housing speakers and microphones." Reportedly, the base sits "flush against the wall, positioned beneath the screen."

To read the full Bloomberg report, head over and check it out for yourself. What are your thoughts on Apple's home hub product? Planning to buy one or several? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
